sentences.en: And so we met up at the sandwich shop, and he was gay.
sentences.zh: 我们在三明治店碰面了，他是同性恋。

sentences.en: And he was gay. And because I mean-- What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 他是个同性恋。因为我的意思是——这是什么意思？

sentences.en: It doesn't mean anything bad. It just means like-- because it wasn't bad.
sentences.zh: 这没什么不好的意思。这只是意味着——因为那不是坏事。

sentences.en: Because we were talking, and he was like, he's been out since he was like, 16 or 17 years old.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在聊天，他说，他从16或17岁起就出柜了。

sentences.en: And I think he was like 25, 26 at the time.
sentences.zh: 我想他当时大概25、26岁。

sentences.en: Maybe a little older. But he was absolutely comfortable with himself.
sentences.zh: 可能再大一点。但他对自己的身份绝对坦然。

sentences.en: He was absolutely assured of himself. Will and Jason dated for a couple of months before they had sex.
sentences.zh: 他对自己绝对充满自信。Will和Jason约会了几个月才发生性关系。

sentences.en: It was a huge step for Will. But when it was over, Will didn't feel the way he thought he would.
sentences.zh: 这对Will来说是巨大的一步。但事情结束时，Will并没有感觉到他想象中的那种情绪。

sentences.en: That sense of devastation that I was like, oh, my gosh I've completely severed my relationship with God didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 那种我以为会有的毁灭感——天哪，我彻底切断了与上帝的关系——并没有发生。

sentences.en: It didn't happen. It didn't happen. No, which was equally weird.
sentences.zh: 并没有发生。并没有发生。不，这同样很诡异。

sentences.en: I'm like, oh. Here I was thinking I was going to be completely destroyed.
sentences.zh: 我想，噢。我还以为自己会被彻底毁灭呢。

sentences.en: And-- It's like you're waiting for the lightning bolt.
sentences.zh: 而且——就好像你在等待闪电劈下来一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it never-- it didn't drop on me.
sentences.zh: 对，而且它从来没有——它没有劈到我头上。

sentences.en: But I mean, I still felt kind of weird. Like, I remember feeling like, well, you've done it now.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，我还是觉得有点怪。我记得当时的感受是，好吧，你现在已经干了。

sentences.en: There is no going back from this experience.
sentences.zh: 这段经历已经没有回头路了。

sentences.en: You're going to have to tell the brothers that you did this.
sentences.zh: 你将不得不把这件事告诉弟兄们。

sentences.en: And he was right. As crazy as this sounds, the very morning after he lost his virginity, Will came home to an email from another witness, an old friend, who had somehow stumbled upon Will's OKCupid profile and was now threatening to out him.
sentences.zh: 他是对的。听起来可能很疯狂，就在他失去童贞的第二天早上，Will一回家就收到了一封来自另一位见证人的邮件，那是他的一个老朋友，不知道怎么回事，这个朋友偶然发现了Will的OKCupid个人资料，现在正威胁要让他出柜。

sentences.en: I mentioned to Will that it seemed to me rather suspicious that this righteous and straight and happily married brother just happened to have discovered Will's men seeking men profile.
sentences.zh: 我跟Will提到，这个正派、正直且婚姻幸福的弟兄竟然“碰巧”发现了Will的男寻找男资料，这让我觉得挺可疑的。

sentences.en: But Will, good-natured as he is, refused to go down that speculative road with me.
sentences.zh: 但Will为人随和，拒绝和我一起进行这种猜测性的探讨。

sentences.en: He said the brother wrote, either you tell them or I will.
sentences.zh: 他说那个弟兄写道，要么你告诉他们，要么我来告诉他们。

sentences.en: And so with the proverbial gun to his head, Will called up one of the elders and told him that he had, as he put it then, a problem.
sentences.zh: 于是，在可以说是大难临头的情况下，Will给其中一位长老打了电话，告诉对方他用他的话说，遇到了一个“问题”。

sentences.en: He was kicked out, officially disfellowshipped.
sentences.zh: 他被踢出了教会，正式开除。

sentences.en: When I was 16 or 17, I gave my mom this long handwritten letter informing her that I had stopped believing in God and that I no longer wanted to be one of Jehovah's Witnesses.
sentences.zh: 在我16或17岁时，我给我妈写了一封长信，亲笔写的，告诉她我不再相信上帝了，我不再想做耶和华见证人了。

sentences.en: I don't remember exactly what was in the letter.
sentences.zh: 我不记得信里具体写了些什么了。

sentences.en: I'm sure I didn't mention that hormones and a sudden vexing need to talk to girls were factors in my decision.
sentences.zh: 我确信我没有提到荷尔蒙以及突然涌现的、想跟女孩说话的迫切需求是我做出决定的因素。

sentences.en: Anyway, I slammed that door really hard, and it became one of the defining choices of my life.
sentences.zh: 总之，我狠狠地把那扇门给关上了，这成了我人生中最具决定性的选择之一。

sentences.en: Shortly after I gave Ma the letter, I flew 3,000 miles away to college, and by the time I stepped off the plane, I was an atheist.
sentences.zh: 把信交给妈妈后不久，我就坐飞机去3,000英里外上大学了，等我走下列车的那一刻，我已经是个无神论者了。

sentences.en: For the most part, I'm relatively proud of everything I've become after that.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，对于后来变成的我，我大体上还是挺引以为傲的。

sentences.en: When I first read Will's email, I couldn't understand why he was holding onto the truth.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次读到Will的邮件时，我不明白他为什么还要抓着“真理”不放。

sentences.en: The Jehovah's Witnesses had publicly slammed the door on who he was and who he was becoming.
sentences.zh: 耶和华见证人已经公开对他是谁以及他正在成为谁关上了大门。

sentences.en: It wasn't that I thought he should be angry, although I felt like he should be a little angry.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说我认为他应该生气，尽管我觉得他多少应该有点生气。

sentences.en: But I wondered why he wasn't free, why he sometimes still thought that Harry Potter was satanic, or that his sexuality was a sin, or why he couldn't just move on.
sentences.zh: 但我纳闷他为什么不觉得自由，为什么他有时依然会觉得哈利·波特是邪恶的，或者他的性取向是一种罪过，为什么他就不能向前看呢。

sentences.en: After talking to Will for a while, it became obvious that it's just not that easy.
sentences.zh: 和Will聊了一会儿之后，很明显，事情没那么简单。

sentences.en: He was a witness for a long time. What he learned won't just go away.
sentences.zh: 他当了很久的见证人。他学到的东西不会凭空消失。

sentences.en: And then something more surprising hit me, a pang of envy.
sentences.zh: 然后，更让人惊讶的感觉击中了我的内心，那是一阵嫉妒。

sentences.en: I was a little jealous of the way Will remembered specific scriptures, even the ones that condemned him.
sentences.zh: 我有点嫉妒Will能记住特定的经文，甚至是那些谴责他的经文。

sentences.en: Were you around for the Knowledge book? Was that the red one?
sentences.zh: 你经历过《知识》那本书吗？那是红色的那本吗？

sentences.en: No, I think that that's the Live Forever book maybe.
sentences.zh: 不，我想那可能是《永远活着》那本书吧。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, yeah. It sounds familiar, but I don't remember which one it was.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，对。听起来很熟悉，但我不记得是哪一本了。

sentences.en: The Knowledge that Leads to Everlasting Life.
sentences.zh: 《导至永生的知识》。

sentences.en: I remember I was reading out of that book when I was a teenager, and I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我记得我十几岁的时候读过那本书，我很喜欢。

sentences.en: Will recalled the details, what the different Jehovah's Witness books were called and their corresponding colors, the meetings, the designations of all the elders.
sentences.zh: Will回忆起各种细节，不同耶和华见证人书籍的名称及对应的颜色，聚会，所有长老的头衔。

sentences.en: I had made turning my back on the truth such a significant part of my identity that I had lost these memories.
sentences.zh: 我把背叛真理变成了我自我认同中如此重要的一部分，以至于我把这些记忆都给弄丢了。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, can we nerd out on Jehovah's Witnesses just a little bit, just a little bit.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我们能稍微聊点关于耶和华见证人的书呆子话题吗，就稍微聊一点。

sentences.en: One thing. Sure. Yeah, totally. I have heard that nowadays, that you don't have to necessarily analyze Scripture anymore.
sentences.zh: 就一件事。当然。好，完全可以。我听说现在，你已经不必非得去剖析经文了。

sentences.en: You just have to read it. I was there for that transition.
sentences.zh: 你只需要读它就行。我经历过那个过渡期。

sentences.en: Oh, OK. Yeah, so then these yahoos are getting up to read through a couple of passages, and I'm just like, man, in my day-- Yeah, back in my day, we had to like, actually know what the Scripture meant.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。对，所以这些蠢货站起来读几段经文，我就想，天哪，在我那个年代——对，在我那个年代，我们必须得真正搞懂经文是什么意思。

sentences.en: I should say in recent years, Jehovah's Witnesses reorganized their meetings again to focus more on understanding and interpreting Scripture.
sentences.zh: 我得说，近年来，耶和华见证人再次调整了聚会结构，将重点更多地放在理解和诠释经文上。

sentences.en: I don't remember half of what I learned in the Kingdom Hall, but there is enough that has stuck with me that still occasionally affects the way I see the world or the decisions I make, even if I don't like to admit it.
sentences.zh: 我不记得我在王国聚会所里学到的一半东西了，但残存的记忆依然够多，偶尔还是会影响我看待世界的方式或我做决定的方式，即便我并不愿意承认这一点。

sentences.en: Will calls it a spiritual aftertaste. Just this morning I had like, something that I really, really, really wanted to happen, and I was hoping it would happen.
sentences.zh: Will把它称为精神回味。就在今天早上，我有件非常非常非常希望它发生的事，而且我盼着它能实现。

sentences.en: And I had a gut feeling of, what can I do about this?
sentences.zh: 我当时有一种直觉：我能为这事做点什么吗？

sentences.en: And the word "pray" came to mind, which is ridiculous for me.
sentences.zh: “祈祷”这个词浮现在脑海里，这对我来说太荒谬了。

sentences.en: I've haven't prayed since I was 17 years old.
sentences.zh: 我从17岁起就再也没祈祷过了。

sentences.en: And it's like, I don't believe in the power of prayer.
sentences.zh: 而且就好像，我不相信祈祷的力量。

sentences.en: But it's like built into your DNA at a certain point, or like, you know, more into your muscle memory.
sentences.zh: 但这就好比在某个阶段被写入了你的DNA，或者说，更多地融入了你的肌肉记忆。

sentences.en: And it just-- it made me actually angry to feel that way because I try to be self-determined.
sentences.zh: 而且它——这种感觉让我其实很生气，因为我总是努力让自己保持独立自主。

sentences.en: Yeah. It's almost like, I think if you think of in terms of military training, you kind of react to situations based on what your training has told you.
sentences.zh: 对。这几乎就像是，如果你从军事训练的角度来思考，你对情况的反应基本上是基于你的训练给你的本能反应。

sentences.en: After I quit, my mom sent me a few long handwritten letters urging me to come back to the Kingdom Hall.
sentences.zh: 我退教后，我妈给我寄了几封长信，都是亲笔写的，劝我回王国聚会所去。

sentences.en: At least, I think that's what they said.
sentences.zh: 至少，我想信上写的是这个。

sentences.en: I never read any of them. I felt like I had made my decision, and I hated that she questioned it.
sentences.zh: 我一封也没读。我觉得我已经做出了决定，而且我很讨厌她对此产生质疑。

sentences.en: These days, when I see Jehovah's Witnesses in the street handing out material, I sometimes go rigid and quickly look away.
sentences.zh: 如今，当我在街上看到耶和华见证人发传单时，我有时会浑身僵硬，然后迅速把头转开。

sentences.en: I just don't want to deal with it. I picked a side.
sentences.zh: 我只是不想跟他们打交道。我选好了立场。

sentences.en: But Will stands halfway between them and me.
sentences.zh: 但Will站在他们和我的中间。

sentences.en: He's half in and half out. Somehow, that made it possible to look back for a couple of hours, to remember that it meant something to me then without it having to mean something to me now.
sentences.zh: 他半推半就，身处两边。不知怎么的，这让他能够回首过去几个小时，去回想它在当时对我意味着某种意义，而不必强求它在现在对我也依然意味着什么。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由Dana Chivvis制作。

sentences.en: Our staff includes Elna Baker, Susan Burton, Ben Calhoun, Zoe Chace, Sean Cole, Whitney Dangerfield, Neil Drumming, Stephanie Foo, Kimberly Henderson, Chana Joffe-Walt, David Kestenbaum, Seth Lind, Miki Meek, Robyn Semien, Christopher Swetala, Matt Tierney, Julie Whitaker, and Diane Wu.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作人员包括Elna Baker、Susan Burton、Ben Calhoun、Zoe Chace、Sean Cole、Whitney Dangerfield、Neil Drumming、Stephanie Foo、Kimberly Henderson、Chana Joffe-Walt、David Kestenbaum、Seth Lind、Miki Meek、Robyn Semien、Christopher Swetala、Matt Tierney、Julie Whitaker和Diane Wu。

sentences.en: Our senior producer is Brian Reed.
sentences.zh: 我们的资深制作人是Brian Reed。

sentences.en: Gerald Murnane, the Austrian novelist I talked to at the beginning of the show, he's the author of The Plains and other books.
sentences.zh: Gerald Murnane，我在节目开头采访的那位澳大利亚小说家，他是《平原》及其他书的作者。

sentences.en: He has not one, but two books coming out here in the States soon.
sentences.zh: 他很快不仅有一部，而是两部书要在美国出版。

sentences.en: One is Border Districts. The other Stream System-- The Collected Short Fiction of Gerald Murnane.
sentences.zh: 一部是《边境地区》。另一部是《溪流系统——Gerald Murnane短篇小说集》。

sentences.en: Our website, thisamericanlife.org. This American Life is delivered to public radio stations by PRX, the Public Radio Exchange.
sentences.zh: 我们的网址是thisamericanlife.org。《This American Life》由PRX（公共广播交易所）分发给各家公共广播电台。

sentences.en: Thanks as always to our program's co-founder, Mr.
sentences.zh: 一如既往地感谢我们节目的联合创始人，Mr.

sentences.en: Torey Malatia. You know, he's still wearing those special glasses that he bought to watch the eclipse.
sentences.zh: Torey Malatia。你知道的，他还在戴着他买的那副来看日食的特殊眼镜。

sentences.en: He says they are so powerful. And I can watch and see rainforests get destroyed, or I can see politicians come into office and do terrible things to people.
sentences.zh: 他说这眼镜太厉害了。我可以看着雨林被毁，或者我可以看到政客上台对人们做可怕的事情。

sentences.en: I'm Ira Glass. Back next week with more stories of This American Life.
sentences.zh: 我是Ira Glass。下周将带回更多《This American Life》的故事。
